govwin role guide · RFP Admin

Run the Platform, End-to-End

The operator's journey: monitor sources, ingest and curate RFPs, push opportunities to customers, release their purchases, and oversee every workflow and agent from one console.

Screenshots are the live admin console. Where a customer's work needs a hand, you shadow-descend into their portal, do the work, and rise back up to ingest more — all as one account.

master_admin holds global access · every action is audited

Sign in & the admin landing

where /admin · sign in as eric@rfppipeline.com

Sign in as your RFP-admin account. The landing is role-aware: it opens the operations console with your live ToDos — purchases awaiting curation, RFPs mid-triage, and workflows parked on a human gate.

The seeded operator eric@rfppipeline.com is a master_admin: global access to every tenant plus the full admin surface. No per-tenant grant needed — it can dip into any company and rise back up to ingest.

Setup — source monitoring & scouts

where /admin/sources · /admin/sources/<id> · /admin/scouts

Before anything is ingested, point the platform at where opportunities live. Sources defines the sites and feeds to watch; Scouts is the worker pool that visits them on a schedule, diffs the results, and surfaces new or changed solicitations. Configure regions to watch, run a scout on demand, and review the diffs.

The scout worker pool

where /admin/scouts

The scout pool shows each worker, its schedule, last run, and yield. Scouts run managed and audited — a run that fails on one source continues on the others. Newly discovered solicitations land in the intake queue for triage.

Ingest — upload an RFP

where /admin/rfp-curation/upload

To bring a solicitation in by hand, use Upload. Drop the solicitation PDF(s); the ingestor extracts text (with an ingest-assist pass), de-duplicates against existing solicitations, and stages the documents in object storage. It handles multi-document packages and marks a primary.

Malformed source PDFs (odd fonts, embedded control characters) are sanitized on the way in — the atomizer and ingestor strip invalid bytes so a bad file can't poison downstream text.

Curate — triage, topics, compliance, skeleton

where /admin/rfp-curation · /admin/rfp-curation/<solId> · .../topic/<topicId>

Curation is the heart of the operator's work. Open a solicitation to triage it, extract its topics (umbrella + every sub-topic), attach the compliance requirements (from a preset or suggested), and build the section skeleton that becomes each proposal's matrix. Apply a preset to one topic or fan it to all.

Verified on DON26BX03-NP002: triaged, topics extracted, the DON 6-volume CSO compliance attached, and the Technical Volume 2 skeleton linked to its template mold.

Templates & molds studio

where /admin/templates · /admin/templates/<id>/edit

The Template Studio is where section molds live — the format contracts (page limit, margins, font, required structure) a required item points at. Author a template on the canvas, or templify a winning past proposal into a reusable skeleton, then attach it to a compliance item so every provisioned proposal inherits the right shape.

Push opportunities to customers

where /admin/opportunities · /admin/cards

When a solicitation is curated, push it. The push fans every activated opportunity (umbrella + all topics) across the forward-only opportunity bridge into a denormalized card for every tenant, auto-scored against each tenant's buckets on arrival. This is the discovery release — customers now see the opportunity ranked in their pipeline.

Verified: the C-UAS topic pushed to Immobileyes ranked #1 in their pipeline within the same run.

Purchases & the curation release (72h SLA)

where /admin/purchases · /admin/applications

When a customer buys a proposal portal with a comp code, it lands in Purchases as curation_pending with a 72-hour SLA. You release it from the shadow account: releasing provisions the build unlocked and instantiates the compliance matrix + molds from the master solicitation. This is the second release over the bridge — the proposal-portal build.

Monitor — the workflow catalog & instances

where /admin/workflows

Every automation runs as a managed workflow — no fire-and-forget. Workflows is the canonical control surface: the roster of templates with an activation toggle, plus live instances with a per-step progress bar, transition timeline, and outcomes. A step that fails continues on independent branches; a human gate (HITL / ToDo) parks the instance until you advance it.

From an instance you can advance, retry, or cancel. A paused instance shows exactly which gate it's waiting on and who it's assigned to.

Monitor — the agent workforce

where /admin/agents · /admin/guardrail-defaults

Agents is the workforce roster: each archetype, whether it's awake, and its per-tenant usage over the forward-only bridge. Tenant-space agents are tenant-bound and advisory — they propose, a guardrail checks, and a human accepts; they never auto-write business tables. Guardrail defaults sets the safety envelope (round/cost/rate/budget caps) every agent runs inside.

Monitor — events, automation, processes

where /admin/events · /admin/automation · /admin/process · /admin/processes

Cross-board observability: Events is the immutable stream (every state-changing action emits start→end); Automation is the rules engine with its run logs; Process / Processes are event-based monitors of active instances. Use these to answer “what happened, when, and did it finish?” for any run on either side of the bridge.

Naming overlap to know: /admin/process (event monitor), /admin/processes (instance ledger), and /admin/workflows (canonical) view the same runs. Treat /admin/workflows as primary.

Monitor — system state & analytics

where /admin/system-state · /admin/analytics · /admin/storage

System state is the health board (services, storage, migrations); Analytics rolls up usage across tenants and opportunities. Together they tell you the platform is healthy and where the activity is.

Tenants oversight & shadow-descend

where /admin/tenants · /admin/tenants/<id>

Tenants is the roster of every company on the platform. From a tenant you can review its state, backfill its cards, and — the operator's superpower — shadow-descend into its portal to do work on its behalf (build a library, draft a section, unstick a proposal), then rise back up to the admin surface to ingest more. The session rewrites to tenant_admin inside the portal and a shadow banner marks the descent; every action stays audited.

Verified: eric@rfppipeline.com descends into /portal/immobileyes/* (shadow banner shown), works the proposal, and returns to /admin. One account, both jobs.

govwin role guide · Customer Admin

Build a Winning Proposal, End-to-End

The customer's eight-step journey through the govwin proposal portal — from a ranked opportunity to a submission-ready, downloadable proposal.

Every step below was verified on a real effort: the Immobileyes NAVAIR/NAVSEA Counter-UAS SBIR (topic DON26BX03-NP002). The screenshots are that live run.

Verified end-to-end · every step through the platform's real tools & agents

Sign in & your portal

where /portal/<company>/dashboard

Sign in with the credentials your RFP-Pipeline admin issued. Your dashboard is role-aware: it opens on your company's workspace and surfaces your live ToDos — opportunities to review, proposals in progress, and anything waiting on you.

Find your opportunity (ranked cards)

where /portal/<company>/cards

The Opportunity Pipeline shows every opportunity the platform has pushed to you, ranked by your Spotlight buckets. Each card carries the agency, program, and close date. Pin copies the solicitation's documents into your workspace; Build opens the proposal workspace.

In the verified run, the NAVAIR/NAVSEA Counter-UAS topic DON26BX03-NP002 ranks #1 for Immobileyes — the best fit for a counter-drone optics company.

Set your scoring criteria (buckets)

where /portal/<company>/buckets

Spotlight buckets are your scoring criteria — the themes you care about (e.g. “Counter-UAS”, “AI sensor fusion”). Every card is scored against each bucket, and editing a bucket re-ranks your pipeline automatically. This is deterministic today; an optional scoring agent overlays it later.

Build your content library (upload → atomize)

where /portal/<company>/atoms · Upload package → atomize-package

Your library is the raw material every draft is built from. On Library → Upload package, drop your past proposals, capability docs, résumés, and data (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX). The atomizer deconstructs each file into a reference atom (the whole doc) plus one primitive atom per substantive block, and auto-tags them against the shared taxonomy (volume, kind, agency, program, phase).

Verified: five Immobileyes documents (GHOST draft, TACFI Technical Volume, résumés, foreign affiliations, cost proposal) atomized into 24 atoms — tagged vol:technical vol:cost vol:key_personnel kind:bio and more. Each uploaded package also gets a “Save as template” button (templify) to reuse its winning structure.

Group atoms & arrange the canvas

where /portal/<company>/atoms · section canvas → “+ From Library”

Atoms aren't just a flat list. In the library, select several primitives and Group into new atom to compose a reusable bundle — a “Team for Navy” group, a past-performance set. Inside a section, “+ From Library” inserts atoms straight into the canvas as nodes, and you drag to reorder them into the flow you want.

Verified: three GHOST past-performance & partner primitives composed into one group, inserted into the Related Work section, then reordered on the canvas.

Open the proposal & compliance matrix

where /portal/<company>/proposals/<id>

Opening a proposal provisions the full compliance matrix — every required volume and item the solicitation demands, each linked to a section “mold” that carries the format rules (page limit, margins, font). The specific agency template is built into the matrix, so the structure is correct before you write a word.

Verified: the DON 6-volume CSO structure (Cover · Technical · Cost · CCR · Supporting · FWA), with Volume 2 aligned to the DON Phase-I Open-Topic Technical Volume 2 template (8 sections).

Draft each section with the AI agent

where proposal.draft_section (“Draft all sections”)

Open a section and click Draft (or Draft all sections). The drafting agent reads the RFP context and the section's compliance mold, pulls the most relevant atoms from your library, and writes canvas content sized to the page budget — you review, pick atoms, and revise in the canvas editor. Nothing auto-commits: it's advisory until you accept.

Verified: the proposal.draft_section agent tool ran on all 8 Technical-Volume sections, grounded in the atomized library, applying its budget/fit check (≈ a 2-page, ~1,090-word target per section).

Accept & Lock → the matrix turns green

where lockSectionCore (Accept & Lock)

When a section is right, Accept & Lock it. Locking flips its compliance row to “satisfied,” snapshots the version, harvests reusable content back into your library, and rolls the volume up. When every section of a volume is locked, the volume shows ✓ Volume locked and downloads unlock.

Verified: locking via lockSectionCore turned 10 matrix rows green (8 Technical + 2 Cost). Volume 2 reads “8/8 locked · 9/10 pages · ✓ Volume locked.”

Export your downloadables

where Download Proposal (.docx) · Cost Volume (.xlsx)

With the volume locked, Download your deliverables. The Technical Volume exports to a submission-ready .docx (US-Letter, 1″ margins, the agency's fonts, figures inline and captioned). The Cost Volume exports to an .xlsx with live formulas.

Verified deliverables: a 10-page Technical Volume .docx (6 figures, 5 tables, all 8 DON TV2 sections) and a Cost Volume .xlsx — Base $199,502 ≤ $200k, Option $114,464 ≤ $115k, formulas live.

govwin role guide · Collaborator

Contribute to a Proposal, Scoped to You

You've been invited to help on one proposal. This guide is your whole world in the platform: what you can open, how you contribute in the canvas, and where your assignments live.

Collaborators are stage-scoped — your grant is per-proposal and per-permission (view, comment, or edit). You see exactly what you were invited to, and nothing else.

Scoped access · your grant is enforced by the platform

Accept your invite & sign in

where deep-linked invite email → /login

You'll receive a deep-linked invite email from the company that wants your help. Following it sets up your account and drops you at sign-in. Once in, your identity is tied to that company as a collaborator on the specific proposal(s) you were added to.

An invite is per-proposal. If you're invited to more than one, you'll pick which company/workspace is active when you sign in (one email can hold several memberships).

Your landing — only your assigned work

where /portal/<company>/proposals

Unlike a customer admin, your home is the proposals list scoped to you — the platform redirects you straight to the work you were invited to. You won't see the company's full dashboard, its whole pipeline, or its library; you see your assignments.

Captured behavior: a collaborator opening the dashboard or activity is redirected to /portal/<company>/proposals. If nothing's assigned yet, you'll see the empty assigned-work state until an admin adds you to a proposal.

Open the proposal workspace

where /portal/<company>/proposals/<id>

Open a proposal to see its compliance matrix and sections. What's actionable depends on your grant: with view you can read the state and the drafts; with comment or edit, the section canvas opens for you to contribute. Locked sections are read-only for everyone.

Contribute in the canvas

where /portal/<company>/proposals/<id>/sections/<sectionId>

If your grant includes edit, open an unlocked section and work in the same canvas editor the customer uses — headings, text, lists, tables, and images as structured nodes. Your edits save to the shared draft; the section owner reviews and, when it's right, Accept & Locks it.

You contribute to drafts — you don't lock volumes or export the final package. Those are the customer admin's controls. Once a section is locked it's read-only.

Comment & suggest

where section canvas → comments

With a comment grant (or alongside edit), leave comments on a section to raise questions, suggest changes, or sign off. Comments thread against the section and can be resolved by the owner. This is how a reviewer contributes without changing the draft directly.

Track your assignments

where /portal/<company>/proposals (assigned work)

Your assignments surface as ToDos on your scoped landing — sections waiting on your edit, comments awaiting your reply, reviews assigned to you. Work them down; when a section you own is accepted and locked, it drops off your list.

Scope boundaries — what's out of reach

where redirects / access checks

By design, a collaborator cannot see the company's library and atoms, its Spotlight buckets, its billing, or opportunities it hasn't invited you to. Navigating to those routes redirects you back to your proposals. This keeps the company's book of business private while still letting you do the work you were brought in for.

Access is a living grant: an admin can widen it (view → comment → edit), narrow it, or revoke it. If your access to a company ends, your collaborator membership there is removed — cleanly, without touching any other company you collaborate with.

Each guide is generated from an editable JSON content file in docs/manuals/guides/ — change the data, re-run docs/manuals/build_guides.py, and the HTML + PDF regenerate. govwin, 2026.
